Falcora Superyacht Concept Takes Inspiration From the Falcon and Stuns With a Look That Is Unreal!
7 photos
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli
Riva Yacht has always been synonymous with some of the world’s most luxurious and high-class yachts and boats. So, for folks looking to create the superyachts of tomorrow, tossing this name onto their design is nothing new. Well, a fresh conceptual design that has hit the scene is the Falcora, bearing the Riva name even though it doesn’t exist, yet.
Folks, the first time I encountered the Falcora, I thought I was looking at some trinket that’s born through the use of some AI software. However, I was so intrigued that I chose to dive deeper, and come to find out, Falcora is actually NOT at all crafted with artificial intelligence but the hands and mind of one Tomás Vartorelli, an industrial designer from Argentina.
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli Now, Riva has nothing to do with the design, but if Falcora ever makes it to the real world, I can’t see it bearing any other name. After all, Riva has been at the forefront of luxury boating and yachting for decades, and if any brand out there would be bold enough to try to build something like Falcora, it might as well be Riva.
Riva ships aren’t the largest out there either and judging by the perspective in the renderings, Falcora is clearly not the sort of ship that’s designed to keep you floating at sea for as long as possible, but rather, one that’s to be used to brandish two things: luxury and speed, even if for short bursts at a time.
I mean, every corner of this concept screams speed, with a hull that showcases shapes and cues typically spotted on supercars, maybe even F1 rides. The Falcora gets its name from the “falcon,” and everything about this species of bird is speed and precision .
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli Since all we have here is nothing but a visual exploration of design, and only the exterior, for that matter, we can start by shedding light upon the main line of the hull. When looking at the profile of the Falcora, we can see the central line flowing from the bow to the beach club, low on the ends, and rising higher in the center, giving off a shape that follows that of the beak of a falcon, maybe even its entire head.
Speaking of beaks, falcons also have those wicked nostrils, which I like to see as the turbo intakes of this magnificent natural machine of the skies, and these nostrils and their bone tubercles seem to be expressed in the shape of the individual windows integrated into the hull.
Because of this curvature to the hull, the outdoor space sitting on top may lead you to believe that it follows the same curve but doesn’t. Only the hull itself follows these lines, and this outdoor patio includes a teak flooring that does run flat. I mean, picture trying to enjoy a glass of bubbly on a curved surface as this boat rocks back and forth on the waves underneath.
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli What I'm trying to figure out is how guests transition to the rear of the Falcora or the wheelhouse and main living area. But hey, as a concept, some aspects of the design are clearly not expressed or even worked out.
But, as a concept, however, designers are able to explore all sorts of ideas that we normally wouldn’t see in the real world, be it because they’re too hard to pull off, would be extremely expensive to do so, or are simply impossible to achieve. The windshield is one of those ‘impossible’ traits, with is oddly curved shape, pinched corners, and multi-axis curvature.
The superstructure that rises from the hull to above the wheelhouse is also one of those ‘impossible’ features, again, with wild lines and curves that give this ship its unique and eye-catching looks.
At the very rear of the Falcora, Vartorelli did add another outdoor space, this time, to be used for some dining, maybe even dancing under the stars , and last but not least, the presence of a beach club means that daytime fun is in the works too.
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli The rest of Falcora is, as mentioned, a mystery, with no images showcasing any exploration into lounges, staterooms, luxury bathrooms, or any other space that we find inside such vessels. This side of the story is to be explored and defined when and if this one is ever commissioned for by some billionaire.
Come to think of it, there is a clear client that I say would be interested in the Falcora and if you’re aware of the culture that revolves around the falcon in the Arab world, we could clearly see some oil sheikh showing off their wealth by cruising the coast the Palm Jumeirah or Monte Carlo aboard this yacht. I wouldn’t be surprised to see a couple of falcons circling around Falcora either.
The downside of this visually appealing design is that ship-building methods don’t seem to be able to execute something like this, because if it could, we’d be writing about it. Oh, and if the current state of the industry CAN pull something like this off, it’s bound to cost countless millions of dollars.
